as_told.title: Vanderbilt study links transients to nuclear tests

plain: Brief points of light, called transients, appear and then vanish on photographic plates from the Palomar sky survey, a 1950s photographic map of the night sky. According to a study, they turn up more often around the time of nuclear bomb tests. Michels says the work of the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel found them '68% more likely to show up within 24 hours of a nuclear detonation.' Villarroel and the Vanderbilt researcher Steven Bruel, who wrote the paper in the journal Scientific Reports, tell it more cautiously. Bruel says almost 19% of days after a test have a transient, and Villarroel calls the link 'weak, but it's there and it's statistically significant'. They also tie it to UFO reports in a catalogue kept by the Center for UFO Studies. If true, it would suggest something in orbit was paying attention to nuclear tests.
